$comment: Hard numbers the site quotes, each with its source in the ai-memory repository. Pages read them from here; prose that repeats a number lives in the catalogs, and `npm run check:upstream` lists every sentence that does.

benchmark.source: docs/benchmarks/README.md, docs/benchmarks/longmemeval-s-3.1.2-release.md (the headline numbers) and docs/benchmarks/longmemeval-s-decomposition-2026-10-12.md (the stream off/on table)
columns: full text plus the observation stream (3.1.2, default)
local embeddings plus the observation stream (3.1.2)

stream.comment: Historical October 12, 2026 decomposition experiment, docs/benchmarks/longmemeval-s-decomposition-2026-10-12.md. Stream off then on, same build, 470 questions. p95 in ms; tokens are mean context tokens of the top five hits. This table was not rerun for 3.1.

capCheck.comment: Same report: pages holding exactly the captured text against whole raw sessions, component numbers.

quality.source: AGENTS.md, docs/ and the test attributes in crates/, counted at the release tag by scripts/check-upstream.mjs
quality.directivesNote: List items in the six rule sections of AGENTS.md: build and test commands, code style, cross-cutting invariants, testing, security, maintenance.
quality.testsNote: #[test], #[tokio::test], #[rstest] and similar attributes under crates/*/src (unit) and crates/*/tests (integration). A cargo run reports more because parameterised tests expand into several cases.

release.comment: The version the written highlights in download.json describe. check:upstream fails when a newer release exists, so the summary is rewritten at every sync.
